<context_for_action>
The apt-get install command timed out during package download (memory entry [00000012]). The installation was terminated after downloading approximately 59 packages, but before completion. 

Before proceeding with the configure script, you need to verify whether gcc and build tools were successfully installed despite the timeout. The memory bank notes that gcc availability is uncertain — the installation may be partial.

Check if gcc is now functional before attempting to run ./configure. A simple `gcc --version` or `which gcc` will confirm availability. If gcc is still missing, you may need to:
1. Resume or retry the apt-get install with a longer timeout
2. Or install just the essential packages individually (gcc, make) to reduce download time

The configure script will fail again with "No working C compiler found" if gcc isn't properly installed.
</context_for_action>
